newsitem.title: JAPAN: Russia PGM exports to Japan to resume soon - traders.
newsitem.headline: Russia PGM exports to Japan to resume soon - traders.

text.p: Russia's platinum group metals (PGM) export agency Almazjuvelirexport (Almaz) has informed Japanese clients that PGM shipments, suspended since January, will resume soon, traders said on Wednesday.
Traders said they had been informed by Almaz that shipments under long-term contracts were likely to resume in June, while spot market sales would start at an even earlier date.
"Almaz has asked our office in Moscow how much (PGM) we would need for 1997," a trading house trader said.
Almaz has assured Japanese clients that Russia can provide the same volume of PGMs as last year, traders said.
In Moscow on Tuesday, the agency said in a statement it had started talks with customers on 1997 exports of PGMs, such as platinum and palladium.
Almaz officials are expected to visit Japan by early June to hold term contract negotiations, although a time schedule has yet to be finalised, traders said.

"The shipments expected in June will be conducted through a tentative agreement, probably through fax. After that, a Russian mission will come to Japan to sign official documents," an official at a major bullion house said.
Some Japanese precious metal traders, who are due to attend a platinum convention in London next week, are now in Moscow to negotiate PGM sales, traders said.
Russia is the world's largest palladium supplier and second largest platinum supplier, while Japan is the world's largest consumer of those precious metals.
Russian sales of PGM have been suspended since the beginning of this year due to domestic problems, such as a cabinet shake-up and delays in passing the 1997 federal budget.
